meta.tagline: The emerald city of coffee steam, ferry horns and mountain views

overview.title: Welcome to Seattle
overview.intro: Seattle is an emerald strip squeezed between two waters: the ferries of Puget Sound on one side, Lake Washington on the other, and on the horizon Mount Rainier appearing and vanishing among the clouds. This city gave the world coffee culture, grunge and software giants, yet its daily life still flows at the market stall, on the ferry deck and in the neighborhood coffee shop. The rain's reputation is exaggerated — it drizzles and passes; locals don't even carry umbrellas. And when 'the Mountain is out', everything about the day is good.

local_word.definition: The local phrase announcing that Rainier has emerged from the clouds. The 4,392-meter volcano hides most days; on the morning it appears, the sentence circulates through offices, buses and cafes. When you hear it, run to a window — Seattle's finest days open with these words.

rules.title: Hit Pike Place in the morning, skip the first Starbucks queue
rules.description: At 09:00 the market crackles with setup energy; by noon it's shoulder to shoulder: see the fish throwing, the flower stalls and the craft tables in morning calm. The 'first Starbucks' queue can run an hour — inside is an ordinary store; drink your coffee at the city's independent roasters.

rules.title: Drop the umbrella, wear layers
rules.description: Seattle rain is drizzle, not downpour: locals wear hooded jackets, and an umbrella marks the tourist. A waterproof layer and walking shoes suffice — drizzle doesn't cancel plans; it converts them into coffee breaks.

rules.title: Board a ferry — the destination barely matters
rules.description: The Puget Sound ferries are the city's finest 'tour': the Bainbridge run serves skyline, mountains and gulls in 35 minutes. Walk-on tickets are cheap — cross over, drink a coffee in the town, and meet the sunset on the deck coming home.

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: Market stalls and a volcano skyline

quick_facts.label: Language
quick_facts.sub: Polite but reserved: the Seattle Freeze

tip.label: The Seattle philosophy
tip.text: This city lives not by the weather but despite it: walks in drizzle, coffee under clouds, everyone outdoors in sun. Keep plans flexible and bolt outside at the sunbreak — Seattle days are beautiful in fragments, and the fragments must not be missed.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Seattle is a hill city relaxed by rail: the Link train is the spine, the ferries a feast, the neighborhoods walkable islands.

items.title: Arriving from the airport
items.description: From Sea-Tac the Link light rail reaches Downtown in 40 minutes: cheap and traffic-free. ORCA card or contactless — a ride app takes 25–50 minutes by traffic; the train wins at most hours.

items.title: Link light rail
items.description: The north-south line runs from the university to the airport: the Capitol Hill and Downtown stops cover a visitor's needs. The expanding network is turning the city rail-first — pick your hotel near the line.

items.title: The ferry network
items.description: Ferries leave Colman Dock for Bainbridge and Bremerton all day: walking on is cheap and effortless. The deck can be cold — the view repays the jacket with interest.

items.title: Hill walking
items.description: The Downtown–Pike Place–waterfront triangle is walkable but hilly: the stairs from the market to the shore and the new waterfront promenade make the pleasant route. Capitol Hill and Fremont walk well within themselves.

items.title: The Burke-Gilman Trail
items.description: The old rail line offers kilometers of lakeside cycling: the Fremont-to-Gas Works stretch is the classic. Shared bikes and scooters abound — the best route on a dry day.

callout.label: Ferry tip
callout.text: Walk onto the Bainbridge ferry forty minutes before sunset: the skyline turns gold on the way out and the city lights come on for the return. Stand on the open deck — if Rainier is out, the view triples. This ticket is the city's cheapest miracle.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Seattle the choice is a choice of rhythm: Downtown beside the market, Capitol Hill's night energy, Fremont's odd charm, Ballard's Scandinavian soul.

local_word.definition: The local shorthand for Puget Sound: the glacier-carved inland sea wrapping the city's west. Ferries cross it, orcas swim it, the sun sets into it. A 'Sound-view room' is a status symbol in Seattle — locals even give directions by 'the Sound side'.

items.name: Downtown and around Pike Place
items.description: Walking distance to the stalls, the waterfront and the Link line: the practical base for a first visit. Watching the market set up in the morning is this location's reward.

items.name: Capitol Hill
items.description: Coffee shops, record stores, bars and the city's liveliest night scene: the heart of young Seattle. Two Link stops from Downtown — for seekers of energy and character.

items.name: Ballard
items.description: The old fishing quarter's breweries, Sunday street market and canal locks: it lives at its own small-town rhythm. Strong seafood tables — the calm, characterful side.

items.name: Fremont
items.description: The self-declared 'center of the universe': a troll under the bridge, a Sunday flea market, canal-side walks. Seattle's sense of humor resides here.

items.name: Queen Anne
items.description: The hill neighborhood beside the Space Needle: Kerry Park's famous skyline frame is here. Quiet streets, porch breakfasts — the graceful base for the view-first visitor.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Seattle's secret is in the calendar: July through September is a nearly rainless paradise, and winter is the season of coffee and museums.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Cherry Blossoms and Sunbreaks
items.subtitle: Spring · Blossoming campus, broken sun
items.description: In late March the university quad's cherry trees become a pink dome, and the tulip fields bloom to the north. The weather is fickle: drizzle, sun and rainbow share the same hour — the season of layers and flexibility.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: In early April go to the UW Quad in the morning: Gothic halls under cherry blossoms — the postcard of a Seattle spring. Pair it with the Skagit tulip fields an hour north and the day is complete.

items.label: Summer
items.name: The Dry Season Miracle
items.subtitle: Summer · Sunny 24°C, long evenings, the Mountain always out
items.description: The Seattle summer is America's best-kept secret: July and August run nearly rainless, light until 22:00, and humidity-free. The Mountain is out most days, the lakes are swimmable, the city turns festive — the calendar's golden window.

callout.label: August tip
callout.text: On an August evening sit atop Gas Works Park: lake, skyline and sunset in one frame. For a Rainier day, drive two hours — wildflower season on the Paradise trails falls exactly in these weeks.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Golden Leaves and Salmon
items.subtitle: Autumn · Crimson parks, returning salmon, first drizzles
items.description: October paints the city gold, the salmon return home through the canal locks, and the coffee shops shift to winter mode. The drizzle begins but without drama — a calm, misty, photogenic season.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: Visit the Ballard Locks' fish ladder in October: watch the salmon climb behind the glass — free and mesmerizing. A brewery beer in Ballard afterwards is autumn's proper close.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Coffee and Mist Season
items.subtitle: Winter · Short days, drizzle, steamed windows
items.description: Winter Seattle moves indoors: the cafes fill, the museums quiet down, and the early dark hands over to lit shopfronts. Snow is rare and drizzle constant — the famous 'gray' earns its name in these months, and the coffee is this good precisely because of it.

callout.label: January tip
callout.text: On a drizzly morning draw a coffee map: three independent roasters, three brew methods, record shops and bookstores between. That is the correct reading of a Seattle winter — umbrella-less, hooded, warm cup in hand.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Seattle table is the bounty of cold waters: salmon and oysters, the fresh hum of the market stalls, and the world's most serious cup of coffee.

local_word.definition: Seattle's everyday food signature: the sweet-soy grilled chicken and rice formula born in small shops opened by Japanese immigrant masters in the 1970s. Hundreds of independent teriyaki joints dot the city — cheap, fast and true. What pizza is to New York, teriyaki is to Seattle.

items.name: The coffee ritual
items.description: Starbucks was born here, but the city's heart beats in the independent roasters: single origins, pour overs and latte-art seriousness. Ask the barista 'what are you brewing today' — in Seattle that question is a mark of respect.

items.name: A Pike Place stall crawl
items.description: Fish-throwing counters, the piroshky bakery, a chowder cup and fresh fruit: a standing tour inside the market is the best lunch. Go in the morning — the stalls' setup is the show itself.

items.name: The teriyaki joint classic
items.description: Sweet-soy grilled chicken, steamed rice and cabbage salad: the set meal of the neighborhood teriyaki shop. A plain shopfront and full tables — Seattle's everyday democracy of flavor.

items.name: The oyster and salmon table
items.description: Puget Sound oysters on ice, sockeye salmon over coals: the cold waters' bounty on a plate. Oyster-bar happy hour is the city's best affordable luxury — the season's salmon is asked about, never waved off.

items.name: Pho and dim sum in the ID
items.description: The storied kitchens of the Chinatown-International District: steaming pho bowls, dim sum carts and Filipino bakeries. The warmest answer to a drizzly day lives in this neighborhood.

items.name: The doughnut and ice cream scene
items.description: Artisan doughnut shops and local creameries take sweet competition seriously: a lavender or salted-caramel scoop beside your coffee is the signature close.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: Don't join the 'first Starbucks' queue: in the same time you can visit two independent roasters, and both are better. With seafood, the season question earns respect — ask 'which oysters today?' and the answer walks you to the right plate.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone sees the Space Needle; these six are Seattle's ferry-horned, troll-shadowed hidden face.

items.name: Gas Works Park
items.description: The rusted towers of an old gasification plant turned lakeside sculpture: from its hill you watch skyline, sailboats and sunset. Seattle's best-loved lawn — shared with kite flyers and picnicking locals.

items.name: Kerry Park
items.description: The small terrace on Queen Anne hill: the Space Needle, the skyline and, on a clear day, Rainier in one frame. The postcards are shot from here — take your place twenty minutes before sunset.

items.name: The Ballard Locks
items.description: The ship locks between sea and lake, with a fish ladder alongside: as boats rise, salmon climb behind the glass. Free, engineering and nature on one stage — with a botanical garden thrown in.

items.name: Discovery Park
items.description: The city's largest park: forest trails descend to a cliff-lined shore, and the Sound opens at the West Point lighthouse. The two-hour loop delivers wilderness without leaving town.

items.name: The Fremont Troll
items.description: A concrete giant clutching a real Volkswagen beneath the Aurora bridge: the neighborhood's monument to humor. Combine with the Fremont market and the Lenin statue — the 'center of the universe' tour wants half a day.

items.name: Bainbridge Island
items.description: An island town 35 minutes by ferry: a bookstore main street, wine tasting rooms and calm coves. The skyline view from the return deck — Seattle's most pleasant half day.

callout.label: View strategy
callout.text: Seattle's views run on the clock: Kerry Park at sunset, Gas Works in late afternoon, the ferry deck at golden hour. And if the Mountain is out, break every plan and run to a viewpoint — a frame with Rainier is Seattle's most precious souvenir.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Seattle is an honest city; its traps are small but time-devouring — know these four.

items.name: The 'first Starbucks' queue
items.description: An hour-long line outside the historic Pike Place store: inside waits an ordinary menu and souvenir cups — a photo stop, not a coffee experience.
items.instead: Photograph the facade and move to an independent roaster two blocks away: the truth of Seattle coffee brews there. The storied counters inside the market are queue-free and better too.

items.name: Mistaking the Needle for the only view
items.description: The Needle ticket is pricey and its view lacks the Needle itself; the queue stretches on summer days.
items.instead: Kerry Park shows the skyline WITH the Needle for free; the Smith Tower's historic observatory is cheaper and full of character. If you do go up, book the sunset slot ahead.

items.name: Touring with an umbrella
items.description: Seattle drizzle renders umbrellas useless: the wind flips them, locals stare, and your hand stays busy.
items.instead: A hooded waterproof jacket and walking shoes: that is the local uniform. Drizzle breaks no plans — when the sunbreak comes the sun is out anyway; keep walking.

items.name: Driving into Pike Place
items.description: The market's narrow streets and pricey garages lock up by noon: the parking hunt devours the market's joy.
items.instead: Come by Link or on foot; if a car is unavoidable, use the waterfront garages. At 09:00 the market offers both parking and stall calm — the late see the crowd, the early see the market.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: In Seattle the best things are either free or early: the market setup, the ferry deck, Kerry Park and the fish ladder cost nothing. Save the budget for coffee, oysters and a Rainier day — the city gifts the rest in drizzle and views.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From market morning to ferry sunset

steps.title: Pike Place at setup
steps.description: Enter as the stalls assemble: fish throwing, flower towers and the first piroshky. Take your coffee from an independent roaster.

steps.title: The waterfront and the aquarium
steps.description: Descend the market stairs to the shore: walk the new promenade, and drop in on the sea otters if you like.

steps.title: Teriyaki or chowder lunch
steps.description: A set meal at a neighborhood teriyaki joint or a chowder cup at the market: Seattle's everyday flavor.

steps.title: Seattle Center and the music museum
steps.description: Monorail to Seattle Center: MoPOP's guitar tower and grunge memory, or Chihuly's glass garden — your choice.

steps.title: The Kerry Park frame
steps.description: Climb Queen Anne: the Needle, the skyline and, with luck, Rainier. The city's postcard is taken from this terrace.

steps.title: The Bainbridge ferry sunset
steps.description: Walk on and take the deck: a golden skyline going out, city lights coming home. Close with a Downtown oyster happy hour.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Market, canals and the Mountain — the full Seattle

steps.title: Classic Seattle
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: market morning, the waterfront, Seattle Center, Kerry Park, the ferry sunset.

steps.title: The northern neighborhoods
steps.description: Fremont in the morning: the troll, a canal walk and coffee; the salmon ladder at the Ballard Locks at noon; brewery beer and shop-browsing in Ballard; sunset on Gas Works hill + dinner in Wallingford.

steps.title: Mountain or island day
steps.description: If skies are clear, a full Rainier day (Paradise trails, wildflowers or snow views); otherwise a Capitol Hill coffee crawl + ID District dim sum + a museum afternoon. The farewell table is coal-grilled salmon — the Mountain on the plate even when hidden.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Seattle speech is soft, wry and entangled with the weather; these five phrases catch the city's frequency.

items.meaning: Rainier is visible and the day just improved — run to a window when you hear it
A break of sun between clouds — the official word of Seattle weather
The name of the city's polite-but-reserved sociability — don't take it personally; offer coffee
Short for Puget Sound — the inland sea of ferries and orcas
The local name for filter coffee — 'just a drip, please' is the plainest, most respected order
